standard.title: Add and subtract within 20
standard.description: Add and subtract numbers within 20, using physical and virtual materials, part-part-whole knowledge to 10 and a variety of calculation strategies
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can represent practical addition and subtraction situations using materials and counting strategies (AC9MFN05). They can partition and combine collections to 10 using part-part-whole relationships (AC9MFN04). They have not yet applied systematic calculation strategies (counting on, bridging through 10, partitioning) to add and subtract within 20.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students add and subtract numbers within 20 using physical and virtual materials, part-part-whole knowledge to 10 and a variety of calculation strategies.

nodes.label: Counting-on and counting-back strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can add and subtract within 20 using counting-on from the larger number and counting-back strategies, recording with + and − symbols and the equal sign.
nodes.minimum_width: Add two numbers within 20 using counting-on; subtract using counting-back; record one calculation using + or − and = symbols.
nodes.typical_width: Apply counting-on and counting-back strategies consistently within 20; use physical materials and number lines to represent the strategy; record calculations using + and − symbols and the equal sign; connect materials to symbolic recording.
wider: Compare counting-on with counting-all for the same calculation, articulating why counting-on is more efficient and when each strategy might be preferred.
Use virtual number lines to model counting-on and counting-back, comparing the visual jump with the physical count.

response_modes.reason: Students transitioning from counting-all to counting-on need practice to make counting-on the default strategy. The key error — starting the count at the first addend rather than the count after it — requires targeted correction and fluency practice.

nodes.hinge_reason: Counting-on is the baseline strategy required for Node 2 — students who still default to counting-all cannot efficiently apply the bridging-through-10 strategy, which requires holding the first addend as a fixed starting point and partitioning the second.
success_criteria: Applies counting-on correctly for addition within 20 (starts count at the larger number + 1).
Records the calculation using + or − and = symbols.

nodes.label: Bridging through 10
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can add numbers within 20 by partitioning one addend to bridge through 10, using part-part-whole knowledge.
nodes.minimum_width: Partition one addend to make 10 with the other, then add the remainder; record the bridging strategy as a number sentence (e.g. 7 + 5 = 7 + 3 + 2 = 10 + 2 = 12).
nodes.typical_width: Apply bridging through 10 to a range of additions within 20; use physical materials (ten-frames, counters) to model the partition; record the full bridging chain as a number sentence; connect the strategy to part-part-whole knowledge of combinations to 10.
wider: Investigate which additions within 20 can be most efficiently solved by bridging (those that cross 10) versus those best solved by counting-on or using doubles, building a strategic repertoire.
Create story problems that require bridging through 10 and explain why bridging is the most efficient strategy for each.

response_modes.reason: Bridging through 10 relies on automatic knowledge of number combinations to 10. Students who don't yet know, for example, that 7 + 3 = 10 cannot apply the bridge. Using ten-frames and part-part-whole materials in varied contexts helps students see the bridging move as a general strategy rather than a procedure to memorise.

The bridging chain (7 + 5 = 7 + 3 + 2 = 10 + 2 = 12) is a multi-step reasoning sequence. Students need the full chain made visible before they can apply it independently. Recording each step explicitly is the scaffold.

nodes.hinge_reason: Bridging through 10 is a prerequisite strategy for two-digit addition in Year 2 — students who cannot apply it within 20 will lack the foundational move required when adding across decade boundaries. It is also required for Node 3 subtraction strategies that use the think-addition approach.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Bridging through 10 is the conceptual engine of mental addition strategies. Students who understand why it works (because 10 is a landmark number and our number system is base-10) develop transferable reasoning that extends to two-digit addition in Year 2.
success_criteria: Partitions one addend correctly to make 10 with the other when adding numbers that cross 10.
Records the bridging chain with correct number sentences showing each step.

nodes.label: Subtraction strategies within 20
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can subtract within 20 using a range of strategies including counting-back, using related addition facts, and partitioning, choosing strategies based on the numbers involved.
nodes.minimum_width: Subtract within 20 using at least one strategy beyond counting-all; represent using physical materials or a Think Board.
nodes.typical_width: Apply counting-back, think-addition (using known addition facts), and partitioning strategies to subtract within 20; represent story problems on a Think Board; use + and − symbols and the equal sign; explain which strategy was chosen and why.
wider: Explore subtraction through creation and performance of addition and subtraction stories in movement contexts — connecting the mathematical operation to narrative and embodied experience.
Compare 'taking away' and 'finding the difference' as two subtraction interpretations, using the same number sentence to represent both situations.

response_modes.reason: Students often treat subtraction as only 'take away', missing the 'difference' and 'missing addend' interpretations. Varied story contexts are necessary to build the broader concept — the same symbolic subtraction sentence represents multiple real-world situations.

This node integrates counting strategies, part-part-whole knowledge, and symbolic recording into flexible strategy selection. Students need to coordinate all three to solve novel subtraction situations efficiently.

success_criteria: Solves subtraction problems within 20 using a strategy other than counting-all.
Represents a subtraction story problem using a diagram or Think Board and records it with a correct number sentence.
